lessons.title: What tokenomics is actually counting
lessons.content:
# What tokenomics is actually counting

Tokenomics is the policy of a token program: how many units exist, who can create more, who can destroy some, and who is scheduled to receive them. It is not a personality. It is not a guarantee that a chart goes up.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to name total supply, circulating supply, and max supply as three different numbers, and refuse a slide that treats them as one.

## Three supply numbers

Total supply is how many units the contract currently says exist. Circulating supply is how many of those are not locked in a vesting contract, a team wallet labelled as locked, or a similar bucket — and that number is often a dashboard estimate, not a protocol primitive. Max supply is a cap, if the code actually has a cap. Many tokens have no max. Many slides print a max that the mint function can ignore.

## Policy lives in functions

A human-readable whitepaper is not the policy. The policy is mint, burn, pause, snapshot, and the admin that can call them. If mint is public to an owner, supply can rise. If burn is a tax on transfers, supply can fall as people trade. If both exist, you have a tug of war, not a destiny.

## Circulating is a story until proven

Teams count circulating by subtracting wallets they call locked. Locked means a third contract holds tokens until a timestamp, or a CEX wallet is excluded, or a promise. Read the locker. Read the amount. A labelled ‘ecosystem’ wallet is still circulating if it can move.

TABLE
Number | What it is | What it is not
Total supply | Units the contract currently tracks | A promise they will never mint
Circulating | A dashboard’s subtraction | A chain opcode
Max supply | A cap IF the code enforces it | A tweeted round number
Market cap | Price times some supply number | Proof of backing
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** A page says “fixed supply, fully circulating.” You open the explorer. totalSupply can increase via mint(owner). You do not argue with the page. You name the function. You do not send Crystal Stones as tuition. Checkout is USDT BEP-20 on the academy page. Contract to verify only: 0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00.

DIAGRAM
WHITEPAPER SLIDE          CONTRACT STORAGE
  “max 135M”          ->    totalSupply()
  “locked team”       ->    balanceOf(vesting)
  “deflationary”      ->    burn() or tax-to-dead
  Always ask which function matches the word.
ENDDIAGRAM

lessons.title: Who can mint
lessons.content:
# Who can mint

If someone can call mint, supply is a privilege, not a law of physics. Intermediate already taught owner and proxy. Tokenomics starts there.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to find a mint function, name the only address allowed to call it, and say what ‘renounced’ does and does not freeze.

## Mint is a rewrite of totalSupply

mint(to, amount) increases a balance and usually totalSupply. That is new units. They are not mined by your laptop. They are written by whoever the code allows. If that who is a multisig, you still have a who. If that who is a timelock, you have a delay, not a deletion of power.

## Renounce is not a magic word

Renouncing owner sets owner to the zero address for that Ownable slot. A proxy admin on a different slot can still point the address at new bytecode that mints. A hidden minter role in AccessControl can remain. Count roles, not slogans.

## Capped mint vs uncapped

Some contracts refuse mint above a cap. Some cap is a variable the owner can raise. Read whether cap is immutable. Crystal Stones’ published total of 135,000,000 is a claim to verify on the contract, not a reason to buy. Verify at 0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00 on BSC.

TABLE
Phrase | Check | Failure
Owner renounced | owner() == 0x0 AND no proxy admin AND no minter role | Costume
Hard cap | cap is immutable and mint respects it | Cap is a variable
Fair launch | Who received first balances, and can they mint more | Airdrop theatre
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** A token paired with Crystal Stones claims ‘mint disabled.’ You still read mint, owner, proxy, roles on THAT token. Pairing does not inherit Crystal Stones’ rules. Academy checkout remains USDT BEP-20.

DIAGRAM
owner --mint--> totalSupply up, balanceOf(to) up
  proxyAdmin --upgrade--> new mint() maybe
  dead owner + live admin = costume
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
Academy rule: ‘cannot mint’ is a sentence you prove with functions, not with a banner next to a famous ticker.
ENDNOTE

lessons.title: Allocation is a schedule, not a community
lessons.content:
# Allocation is a schedule, not a community

Allocation tables (team 15%, liquidity 20%, public 40%) are a budget. The chain will not enforce the table unless vesting contracts do. A PNG in a whitepaper is not a vest.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to map an allocation row to a wallet or a vesting contract, and say what happens when a cliff ends.

## Rows need addresses

Team, advisors, ecosystem, liquidity, public. Each row should resolve to an address or a set of addresses. If it does not, it is a wish. Ecosystem wallets that can move today are circulating, whatever the pie chart said.

## Cliffs and linear unlocks

A cliff is a timestamp before which a vesting contract will not pay. After the cliff, linear unlocks pay a slice per block or per second. If the ‘vesting’ is just a team EOA, there is no cliff. There is trust.

## Liquidity allocation is not locked LP

Tokens labelled liquidity may be sitting in a deployer EOA waiting to be paired. LP lock is a different object: LP tokens in a locker. Do not merge them.

TABLE
Row | Honest object | Costume
Team 15% | Vesting contract with cliff | A labelled EOA
Liquidity 20% | Pair + locker holding LP | Tokens in deployer
Community 40% | Airdrop contract with a list | A farm that prints more
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** You read Crystal Stones’ published allocation as a claim. You look for vesting addresses on BSC. You do not send tuition in that token. Intermediate is the academy page in USDT BEP-20.

lessons.title: Inflation, burns, and sinks
lessons.content:
# Inflation, burns, and sinks

Inflation is mint over time. A burn is a send to a dead address or a true totalSupply decrease. A sink is a use that removes units from circulating hands without needing a religion about price.

By the end of this lesson you should separate a burn tax, a dead-address send, and a true burn(), and refuse ‘deflationary’ as a complete sentence.

## Burn tax is not automatically deflation

A transfer tax that sends a slice to 0xdead reduces circulating in a dashboard sense. If mint outruns burns, supply still rises. Read both rates. Read whether the owner can change the tax to 99%.

## True burn vs costume burn

burn(amount) that decrements totalSupply is a true burn. Sending to a ‘dead’ wallet that someone might still control is a costume if that wallet is not provably unspendable. 0x000…dead is conventional, not mystical.

## Sinks need a reason to happen

A sink is a product that spends tokens (fees, access, redemption). If nobody uses the product, the sink is a drawing. Academy tuition is not a Crystal Stones sink. Tuition is USDT BEP-20.

TABLE
Word | Mechanism | Abuse
Inflation | mint on a schedule | Silent extra minter
Burn | totalSupply down | Tax that only fills a team wallet
Sink | users spend units | A sink that is actually optional air
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** A farm says ‘deflationary like Crystal Stones.’ You verify Crystal Stones’ actual burn path on 0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00. You do not assume the farm copied it. You do not buy either as a class assignment.

DIAGRAM
mint/block ----> totalSupply up
burn/tx   ----> totalSupply down or dead balance up
net = policy, not destiny
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
Academy rule: deflationary is a net of functions over time, not a sticker.

lessons.content:
# Utility vs governance vs meme

Tokens get used as access, as votes, or as a joke people trade. Most tokens mix the three. Intermediate wants you to name the mix, not to pick a mascot.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to classify a token’s claimed job and say which job the code actually supports.

## Utility is a gate

A utility token is spent or held to use a product: fee discount, access, redemption. If the product works with USDT instead, the ‘utility’ is optional theatre. Crystal Stones’ academy does not require the token to study. Basic is free. Intermediate is USDT.

## Governance is a vote notebook

A governance token weights proposals. Without a governor, timelock, and a treasury that actually obeys, ‘governance’ is a Discord poll.

## Meme is attention

A meme token is allowed to exist as attention. The honesty is to say so. Dishonesty is dressing a meme in RWA language. RWA is a later course. Do not launder a joke through a mineral photograph.

TABLE
Claimed job | Code you should find | Costume
Utility | A spend or hold check in a product contract | A PDF of ‘use cases’
Governance | Governor + timelock + treasury
A telegram straw poll
Meme | Usually just ERC-20/BEP-20
An RWA costume
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** A page says Crystal Stones is utility + RWA + governance. You split the claims. Academy access is not gated by holding it. RWA backing is a claim to verify, not a vault you have audited. Governance needs a governor. Education only.

DIAGRAM
JOBS (can overlap)
[ access gate ] [ vote weight ] [ attention ticker ]
Ask which box has bytecode.
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
Academy rule: three jobs on a slide is not three jobs in code.
ENDNOTE

# Unlock charts are timestamps

An unlock is a time when a vesting program allows transfer. It is not a mystical dump switch the chain flips for drama. It is a clock plus a function.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to teach the title — Unlock charts are timestamps — without a marketing slide.

## The object

An unlock is a time when a vesting program allows transfer. It is not a mystical dump switch the chain flips for drama. It is a clock plus a function. Intermediate treats this as an object with a contract, a function, and an explorer row. If you cannot point at those, you have a vibe. Global learners get the same objects. There is no local exception.

## How you check it

Open the bookmarked explorer on the named chain. Read the function names. Read the roles. Read timestamps on vesting if any. Do not use a search ad. Do not use a chat screenshot as evidence. Evidence is the chain and the verified source, with the caveat that verified is a compiler match, not an audit.

## How it fails

It fails when an admin path exists that the slide omitted, when a tax flips, when a vest is only a labelled EOA, or when someone asks you to skip the explorer because ‘the community already checked.’ Communities are not bytecode.

## What this academy will not do

We will not tell you this object is a reason to buy Crystal Stones or anything else. We will not take tuition in Crystal Stones. We will not ask for a seed to ‘apply tokenomics.’ Staff do not DM unlock calendars that require a payment.
